candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the message XML, including the ds:Signature/ds:SignedInfo/ds:KeyInfo content and therefore the ds:KeyValue (Modulus/Exponent for RSA, DSA parameters, EC point) and the ds:SignatureValue. The attacker also controls the private key used to produce the signature.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked X509Data, X509IssuerSerial, X509SKI, X509SubjectName and KeyName branches: setTokenKey installs the configured PublicKey via setPublicKey for token types other than KeyValueToken, and AbstractSecurityToken.getPublicKey returns that field first, so those identifiers do use the configured key. Checked the no-KeyInfo default-token path: it also receives the configured key correctly. Checked that using the message KeyValue when no verification key is configured is expected/self-asserted behavior and therefore not the issue. Checked that the library emits a KeyValueTokenSecurityEvent exposing the token/public key, so an application could in principle reject the attacker key itself, and that getKey("") in AbstractInboundSecurityToken provides a key-table fallback for secret-key lookups but is not used by the asymmetric getPubKey path. Checked that KeyInfo XML itself is parsed by the caller-supplied (and library-warned) hardened stream reader, so this is not an XML-parsing issue.
candidates.impact: Signature-verification bypass / authentication and integrity forgery for applications using the StAX API with a configured signatureVerificationKey: a remote attacker can make arbitrary content be reported as signed (e.g., forge/alter signed SOAP or WS-Security messages) without possessing the trusted private key, by substituting their own public key in ds:KeyInfo/ds:KeyValue.
candidates.prerequisites: The application uses the StAX/streaming API (InboundXMLSec.processInMessage plus security handlers) to verify signatures of untrusted XML, and configures the expected key via XMLSecurityProperties.setSignatureVerificationKey(PublicKey) (the documented way to supply a verification key when not relying on KeyInfo-selected keys). The attacker's message must contain a ds:KeyInfo with a ds:KeyValue and a SignatureValue that validates under the attacker's private key. The application must not independently veto the KeyValueTokenSecurityEvent emitted by the library.
candidates.root_cause: SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.setTokenKey only calls token.setPublicKey(configuredKey) when the token type is not KeyValueToken; for a KeyValueToken it falls into the else branch and stores the configured PublicKey via token.setSecretKey("", key). AbstractInboundSecurityToken.getPubKey (used for asymmetric signature verification) returns only getPublicKey() and never consults that key table. RsaKeyValueSecurityToken/DsaKeyValueSecurityToken/ECKeyValueSecurityToken.getPublicKey build the key from the untrusted ds:KeyValue whenever the publicKey field is null, so the attacker-supplied key is used for SignatureValue verification instead of the caller-configured trusted key.
candidates.title: StAX signature verification uses attacker-supplied ds:KeyValue instead of the configured signatureVerificationKey
candidates.trace: 1) Inbound message contains <ds:Signature> with <ds:KeyInfo><ds:KeyValue><ds:RSAKeyValue>attacker key</...> and a SignatureValue computed with the attacker's private key. 2) SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.getSecurityToken finds KeyInfoType content TAG_dsig_KeyValue and returns RsaKeyValueSecurityToken (SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.java:64-69, 112-143). 3) setTokenKey sees the configured trusted PublicKey but, because token.getTokenType()==KeyValueToken, takes the else branch and stores the trusted key via setSecretKey("", key) instead of setPublicKey (SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.java:247-252). 4) XMLSignatureInputHandler.XMLSignatureVerifier.retrieveSecurityToken obtains this token and AbstractSignatureInputHandler.createSignatureAlgorithm sees isAsymmetric()==true and calls getPublicKey(algorithmURI, Asym_Sig, id) (AbstractSignatureInputHandler.java:288-289). 5) AbstractInboundSecurityToken.getPubKey returns only getPublicKey() (AbstractInboundSecurityToken.java:152-155); the key table containing the configured key is never consulted. 6) RsaKeyValueSecurityToken.getPublicKey finds the publicKey field null and builds the key from the untrusted ds:RSAKeyValue with KeyFactory (RsaKeyValueSecurityToken.java:55-67; DSA/EC analogues). 7) The SignatureValue over SignedInfo is then verified with the attacker's public key and validates, so the message (and its references/SignedElementSecurityEvents) is accepted as signed despite the different configured verification key.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or test suite was available, so the bypass was not executed. It is not proven whether upstream considers ds:KeyValue tokens to be intentionally self-asserted (in which case an app must vet KeyValueTokenSecurityEvent) versus a defect; the inconsistent treatment of X509 vs KeyValue tokens and the dead key-table storage of the configured PublicKey suggest it is a defect. Also unverified is how downstream consumers such as WSS4J/CXF populate signatureVerificationKey and whether they independently reject attacker-supplied KeyValue identifiers.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-347 Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature (key substitution / verification-key bypass)

coverage_summary: Read the source scopes reported by get_source_scope (548 files) and sampled all major areas: DOM/JSR-105 (org.apache.jcp.xml.dsig.internal.dom), legacy XML Signature (signature, transforms, c14n, algorithms, keys/keyresolver, utils/resolver), StAX streaming processors/transforms/security tokens, XML Encryption (XMLCipher/XMLCipherInput/XMLSecurityStreamReader), configuration (config.xml, security-config.xml, Init), and sample code. Traced key-path logic for signature verification end to end across SecurityTokenFactoryImpl, the KeyValue token classes, AbstractInboundSecurityToken and AbstractSignatureInputHandler. No test sources are present in the snapshot; binary/over-size filters reported none excluded.
limitations: No src/test tree is present, so behavior could not be corroborated against the project's unit/integration tests.
No execution, compilation or dynamic analysis was performed (not permitted); the candidate is source-evidence only, not runtime-confirmed.

Cannot inspect upstream fixed revisions or advisories, so it is not proven that the KeyValue behavior was fixed by a later commit versus being intended behavior requiring an application-side KeyValueTokenSecurityEvent check.
StAX-provider defaults (Woodstox/JDK) for DTD and external-entity processing were assumed when assessing the rejected XXE leads; those leads remain unverified.
Downstream usage (WSS4J/CXF) of XMLSecurityProperties.setSignatureVerificationKey with attacker-controlled ds:KeyValue was not inspected because such code is outside the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in StAX transforms: TransformIdentity.getXmlInputFactory() creates an XMLInputFactory without SUPPORT_DTD=false / IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false (TransformIdentity.java:56-63), and TransformBase64Decode.java:115-119 / CanonicalizerBase.java:374-377 re-parse base64-decoded or buffered attacker XML with it. InboundXMLSec.java:53-57 shows the hardened counterpart.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible XXE (file read/SSRF), but the reference/transform processors are only added after AbstractSignatureInputHandler.verifySignedInfo has validated ds:SignatureValue (AbstractSignatureInputHandler.java:74-75, 336-348), so it requires a key the verifier already accepts; it also depends on StAX-provider defaults for DTD/external entities. Not selected over the verification bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: DOM/legacy XXE when secure validation is disabled: XMLUtils.createDocumentBuilder(validating, secureValidation) only rejects DOCTYPE when secureValidation is true (XMLUtils.java:1049-1061), and it is used with secureValidation from Canonicalizer.canonicalize (Canonicalizer.java:259), XMLSignatureInput.convertToNodes (XMLSignatureInput.java:551), SignedInfo.reparseSignedInfoElem (SignedInfo.java:214) and RetrievalMethodResolver/KeyInfoReferenceResolver.
rejected_leads.reason: Security-relevant but gated by a documented secure-validation switch and largely application-driven; the default-off behavior matches the upstream/JSR-105 design, so it is weaker evidence of a distinct defect than the KeyValue key substitution.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF/local file access via default resource resolvers when secureValidation is disabled (ResolverDirectHTTP, ResolverLocalFilesystem; ResourceResolver.java:101-108 rejects them only under secureValidation).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires secure validation to be off and an XML DSig behavior explicitly covered by that switch; not the strongest candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: KeyInfoReference / RetrievalMethod external dereference and chained-reference handling (KeyInfoReferenceResolver.java, RetrievalMethodResolver.java) can fetch external resources and only block loops under secure validation.
rejected_leads.reason: Same secureValidation/configuration gating as the resolver lead; no distinct memory-safety or verification-bypass evidence found.

rejected_leads.lead: Malformed XPointer/index crashes: DOMURIDereferencer.java:77-81 and Utils.parseIdFromSameDocumentURI assume single quotes; ResolverXPointer.isXPointerId indexes an empty id string; DOMDigestMethod/DOMSignatureMethod call alg.equals on a possibly missing Algorithm attribute.
rejected_leads.reason: Runtime exceptions (StringIndexOutOfBoundsException/NullPointerException) that abort processing; a robustness/DoS lead only, without a demonstrated security-relevant integrity or confidentiality impact beyond failure.

rejected_leads.lead: Reference/transform limits only enforced when secureValidation is enabled (DOMReference.java:217, DOMSignedInfo.java:179, Manifest.java:318), leaving unbounded transform/reference counts for default configurations.
rejected_leads.reason: DoS-hardening gap tied to the secureValidation toggle; no definite defect for a single-candidate submission and the StAX path already has unconditional limits.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Santuario XML Security for Java snapshot (pom version 2.0.3-SNAPSHOT; 548 files: main sources under src/main/java, StAX security config under src/main/resources, sample code/data under samples). The strongest source-supported issue is in the StAX (streaming) signature-verification path: when an application configures XMLSecurityProperties.setSignatureVerificationKey(PublicKey) and the incoming message carries a ds:KeyInfo/ds:KeyValue, SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.setTokenKey deliberately does not install the configured key on a KeyValueToken (the key is only stored in a key table that the asymmetric getPubKey path never queries). The RSA/DSA/EC KeyValue token classes then lazily build the token public key from the attacker-supplied ds:KeyValue, and AbstractSignatureInputHandler.createSignatureAlgorithm verifies ds:SignatureValue with that message-supplied key. The result is a signature/key-substitution verification bypass: an attacker can sign arbitrary SignedInfo with their own private key, embed the matching public key in KeyInfo as ds:KeyValue, and have the library report the signature as valid even though the caller configured a different trusted verification key. This is a candidate lead, not runtime-confirmed; I could not execute tests or inspect the project's test suite (not present in the snapshot).
